events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
The cancellation was made by the rider, so the case enters through NS-0's rider branch, which routes an instant booking to NS-4 [F2][NS-0]. The rider cancelled 2 min 55 s (175 s) after matching at 14:05:00, i.e. inside the 3-minute window, and under NS-4 "all cancellations made within 3 minutes of matching are not chargeable" [F2][NS-4]. The $6.61 fee was nonetheless charged [F5][NS-4], so it must be returned in full [F5][NS-7].

The fee cannot be defended as a rider no-show. NS-1 requires that the driver pressed "I'm Here", that GPS placed him at the pickup point, and that he waited over 3 minutes there [F1][F3][F4][NS-1]. None of these holds: the timeline shows no "I'm Here" tap (driver_pressed_here_at null) and no recorded arrival [F3][F4][NS-1], and the GPS record shows the driver's closest approach was 1685 m, never entering the 200 m pickup radius [F1][NS-1]. The driver's own message and statement concede he was still en route [F8][F10][NS-1], and system records (gps/timeline/fare) govern over statements where they differ [F1][F3][NS-1].

The driver's lateness is not itself the ground of the refund: Ryde publishes no late-ETA free-cancellation right, and NS-8 is informational [F1][F8][NS-4]. The refund rests solely on the sub-3-minute timing [F2][NS-4]. Payment follows NS-7 — a $6.61 voucher, the dispute having been raised on this ticket within 30 days of the trip [F2][F5][NS-7].

No account flag is due. RD-6's flag requires a route-deviation finding with route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 [F15][RD-6]; this is a no-show/over-charge case with no off-route segment, and NS-2's abuse flag is triggered only when the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS shows him away from the pickup point — here no tap was ever made [F4][NS-2]. The driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes are a profile observation and cannot alone decide the case or ground an account action [F15][RD-6].

Safety screen: the chat is two routine messages ("How long will you be?", "About 5 min, traffic"), the driver's statement is a neutral concession, and the complaint is about the fee; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, and traffic data shows no incident [F7][F8][F10][F12][SAFE-1]. No escalation.

Amount: the disputed item is the cancellation fee fixed on the fare record at $6.61 [F5][NS-4]; the trace fixes the amount at the cancellation fee of $6.61, unchanged by surge (1.0×) [F6][NS-4].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7), noting the driver was still 1685 m from the pickup point when the rider cancelled; no account flag.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 2 min 55 s after matching (14:05:00 → 14:07:55), i.e. within the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so no cancellation fee is chargeable.
The $6.61 cancellation fee was nonetheless charged and appears on the fare record, so it must be refunded in full.
Even if the driver had claimed a rider no-show, that claim fails: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform never recorded him at the pickup point.

The GPS record confirms the driver was never within 200 m of the pickup point — his closest approach was 1685 m at the moment of cancellation — so the arrival and waiting conditions of the no-show rule could not be met.
The driver's own written statement admits he was still en route ("I was on my way when the rider cancelled"), which corroborates the GPS and timeline records rather than any arrival claim.
The driver's chat at 14:06 estimated about 5 more minutes, which is consistent with the GPS showing he had not reached the pickup point when the rider cancelled.
The driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days, and this over-charge is a further instance of the same conduct; his account should be sent to Ryde for review alongside the refund.
The chat record is complete and fully timestamped (2 messages, both time-stamped), so there is no missing-evidence ambiguity preventing a decision on this ticket.

weaknesses: The cancellation was made by the rider, not the driver (F2), so the ticket does not enter the no-show branches via a driver cancellation; the correct route is the rider-cancellation rule (NS-4), and the driver-side abuse flag under NS-2 arguably does not apply to a fee the driver did not press for.

The rider did cancel after the driver had accepted and was en route, and the driver's chat (F8: "About 5 min, traffic") plus the mild congestion band on Nassim Road (F11, band 3, 20–29 km/h) may be used by the other side to argue the driver was progressing reasonably, though there is no traffic incident (F12) and no rule in Ryde's policy giving a rider a free cancel for a late ETA.

The fee-waiver request window and voucher form are governed by NS-7 (30 days, voucher not cash), and the rider's 90-day dispute history shows 1 dispute with 0 upheld (F14), which the other side may cite to suggest the rider disputes fees without merit.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled this instant booking 2 minutes 55 seconds after matching (14:05:00 → 14:07:55), which is within the 3-minute free-cancellation window of NS-4, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is not chargeable and must be returned in full.

No valid cancellation-fee exception applies on the driver's side either: NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) fail because the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' (driver_pressed_here_at null) and the platform never recorded him at the pickup point, so the fee cannot be defended as a rider no-show — the fee falls away under NS-4's 3-minute rule.

The refund does not depend on delay: Ryde publishes no 'driver late vs ETA' free-cancellation rule (NS-8 is informational and a driver not yet arrived is expressly not a ground for free cancellation under NS-4), so the rider's ground ('driver was nowhere near') is legally irrelevant — but the outcome is the same, refund_full, because the cancellation fell inside the 3-minute window.
The fee must be returned as a Ryde voucher rather than cash and only if the dispute was raised within 30 days of the trip, per NS-7; this is the sole mechanism for the rider's requested $6.61.

Countervailing facts for a favourable exercise of discretion ($6.61 amount is fixed by NS-4; evidence: fare fact F5): the driver's conduct in this incident shows no abuse of the cancellation/waiting button (no 'I'm Here' tap at all), and his 666 trips in 90 days with an unrelated 2 upheld no-show history (F15) is a profile observation that cannot by itself decide this case.

No safety escalation is warranted: the chat contains only routine messages and no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, and traffic data shows no incident (Nassim Road band 3, 20–29 km/h, fair weather), so the case can be decided on the timeline facts rather than referred to a person.

weaknesses: The system records are against my client on the core issue: GPS shows the driver never entered the 200 m pickup radius (closest approach 1685 m at 14:07:55, F1) and the platform never logged an arrival (F3), so the rider's complaint that he 'was nowhere near' is factually accurate and cannot be contradicted from the record.

The driver's chat message 'About 5 min, traffic' (F8) and his written statement 'I was on my way when the rider cancelled' (F10) concede he had not arrived; under the system-record-over-statement rule this admission plus F1/F3 leaves no mileage in arguing the cancellation was a rider no-show under NS-1.

The driver's 90-day profile already shows 2 upheld no-show disputes (F15); the rider side wears zero upheld (F14). While profile facts cannot decide the case, the pattern gives the judge nothing to distinguish this incident from the earlier ones.

NS-4 is a bright-line rule: because the cancellation was at 2:55 (F2), i.e. inside 3:00, the fee fails regardless of how cooperative the driver was, so the best available outcome is refund_full of $6.61 (voucher, NS-7) and not no_action — no argument in this record can preserve the fee.
